title: ATS Profile Hypothesis V1
description: A corpus-layer hypothesis about which ATS-1 profile governs one section of one source document. 99.6% of the pilot corpus declares no profile because it predates ATS, so profile is an annotation target rather than a property the pipeline resolves (spec Section 14.1 makes profile resolution stage 2, and a stage that cannot execute reports its unavailability rather than a value). This object exists so that a scope, the structural and lexical evidence found in it, and the profiles that evidence is consistent with can be recorded WITHOUT any of them being read as a determination. The record is scoped to a section or context bundle, never to a whole document, because Section 9.4 permits an artifact to compose profiles at section level. `decision.state` is `REVIEW_REQUIRED` on every generated record; only an identified annotator may move it, and no generator may move it for them (Section 13.7).

hypothesis_id.description: Content address of the record body, so two runs over the same bytes produce the same identifier and a changed hypothesis is a different record.

context_bundle_id.description: The context bundle this hypothesis was scoped to, when it was built from one rather than directly from a section of the source document.

repository_group.description: Leakage-control grouping key, carried so a hypothesis can be excluded from a split without re-reading the source artifact.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the document. Present so an annotator can find the scope; it is NOT admissible as evidence for a profile.

revision.description: The revision the scope's line numbers are valid at. Line numbers without a revision point at nothing.

scope.description: The section this hypothesis is about. Section 9.4 permits profile composition at section level, so a document-wide hypothesis would erase a distinction the standard makes.

heading_path.description: The heading stack governing the scope, outermost first. Empty for a document with no headings, or for text preceding the first heading; empty is a real answer, not a missing one.

source_sha256.description: Content hash of the whole document the lines are cut from, so a scope whose source has changed is detectable.

candidate_profiles.description: Every profile the evidence in this scope is consistent with. Two or more entries is the normal case for a mixed artifact and MUST NOT be collapsed to one. An empty array means no admissible evidence was found, which is not the same as having found evidence for no profile.

authority.description: The resolved corpus authority under which this scope's text was read. Recorded because a hypothesis derived from text nobody authorised reading is not usable, and the resolution names which input permitted or blocked it. `declaration_location` is required alongside the value: an operator overlay and a repository's own declaration can resolve identically, and a hypothesis that recorded only the permission would read as though the repository owner had authorised it.

generator.description: What produced the record and from which vocabularies, so a reviewer can tell an evidence set apart from a guess.

evidence_sources.description: Every vocabulary the generator was allowed to match against. A term outside these is not evidence, because a vocabulary invented at the corpus layer would create profile labels the standard does not recognise.

refusals.description: The inferences this generator declines to make, restated on every record so a reviewer reading one record sees them.

basis.description: The evidence that raised this candidate, one entry per distinct observation. A candidate with no basis is a guess, so at least one is required. A filename, a path, or a repository is never a basis: nothing about where a document sits establishes what reader job its prose performs.

status.description: `hypothesis` is the only state a generator emits: ranking candidates by cue count would reintroduce the guess this object exists to avoid. `alternative` and `rejected` are annotator states, recorded here so a reviewer's narrowing survives in the same object rather than in a side channel.

conformance_claim_permitted.description: Whether this identifier may carry a core ATS-1 conformance claim. False for every extension-namespaced profile: Section 3.3 permits experimenting with a reserved profile under a namespace but forbids claiming core ATS-1 profile conformance for it, and Section 9.5 requires the identifier be preserved and reported as unsupported rather than mapped to ASSESS or SPECIFY by similarity.

kind.description: The class of observation. Every kind is structural or lexical evidence read out of the scope's own text; there is deliberately no kind for filename, path, repository, or sibling-document convention.

detail.description: The exact surface that was observed, so a reviewer can check the observation rather than trust it.

vocabulary_source.description: Where the matched term is defined. Only the imported force lexicon, a vocabulary enumerated in a normative schema, and the document's own explicit declaration qualify.

occurrences.description: How many times the surface appears in the scope. Volume is context for a reviewer, never a score: one MUST and forty MUSTs raise exactly one candidate.

decision.description: Who decided the profile, and whether anyone has. Section 13.7 forbids a component from becoming the authoritative adjudicator for its own output, so a generated record is always REVIEW_REQUIRED and a RESOLVED record must name a decider that is not the generator.

state.description: `REVIEW_REQUIRED` is the generated state and the default. `RESOLVED` means an identified annotator selected a profile. `REFUSED` means an identified annotator looked and determined that the evidence supports no profile for this scope — which is a decision, unlike the silence of REVIEW_REQUIRED.

decided_by.description: The identity of the annotator who moved the state. A generator identity here would be self-adjudication.
